summary.description: Aldrin is a synthetic pesticide, appearing as a white crystalline solid in pure form, used to control soil insects and protect wooden structures. It is banned in the EU but still in use in some developing countries.
emission_sources: Application as a pesticide in agriculture and wood treatment (in countries where still permitted)
environmental_impact: Highly toxic to birds and waterfowl through ingestion of contaminated plants or aquatic organisms
Persistent in the environment due to its lipophilic nature and conversion to dieldrin
Capable of traveling long distances in the environment
Causes local extinction of species in affected areas

top_sdg_impacts.SDG15_Life_on_Land: Aldrin is extremely toxic to terrestrial wildlife such as birds and accumulates in the food chain, leading to local extinctions and biodiversity loss.
top_sdg_impacts.SDG12_Responsible_Consumption_and_Produc: Despite being banned in many regions, aldrin continues to be used in some countries, highlighting a failure in global coordination for responsible chemical management.
top_sdg_impacts.SDG6_Clean_Water_and_Sanitation: Aldrin’s persistence and mobility through soil and water can contaminate water sources, threatening the safety and cleanliness of drinking water.
